                    ### Question
                    The hairy cell leukemia (hairy cell leukemia) presents as characteristic clinical-biological features:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Lymphocytosis in peripheral blood greater than 50,000 lymphocytes / microL.
opb. T lymphoid line markers
opc. Exfoliative generalized erythroderma, plaques and skin tumors.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Hairy cell leukemia (HCL) is characterized by specific clinical and biological features. The most relevant findings include: 1) Pancytopenia and splenomegaly are common, as the disease often leads to bone marrow infiltration and splenic enlargement, aligning with a consensus of 90%. 2) Lymphocytosis can occur, but counts greater than 50,000 lymphocytes/microL are not typical; thus, this option is less reliable (85% confidence). 3) HCL is associated with B-cell markers rather than T lymphoid markers, making the presence of T lymphoid line markers incorrect (80% confidence). 4) Skin manifestations such as exfoliative generalized erythroderma and plaques are rare and not characteristic of HCL, thus this option is less typical (60% confidence). The evidence path linking pancytopenia to splenomegaly supports the consensus that these features are commonly observed in HCL.
